record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: A semi-dispersive billiard table is obtained from a polygon by replacing some sides by smooth boundary components that are convex inward, while any remaining straight sides are neutral components; a semi-dispersive polygon is the special case where the dispersive components are circular arcs. Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic? Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: These are the semi-dispersive billiard tables. In the absence of neutral components, we speak of dispersive billiard tables.
Problem 4. i) Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic? ii) Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar billiards defined as follows. Start with a (not necessarily convex) polygon in the plane and replace some subset of its sides by smooth curves that are strictly convex when viewed from inside the table (i.e. dispersing/inward-convex boundary components); the sides that remain straight are called neutral components. The resulting region is called a semi-dispersive billiard table. In the special case where every dispersing component is a circular arc, the table is called a semi-dispersive polygon. The billiard flow is the free motion of a point particle inside the table with elastic reflections off the boundary; it is called hyperbolic if its Lyapunov exponents are nonzero almost everywhere with respect to Liouville measure.

(i) Is every semi-dispersive billiard table (as above) hyperbolic?
(ii) Is every semi-dispersive polygon hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether all semi-dispersive billiard tables (and the subclass of semi-dispersive polygons) are hyperbolic is posed as a problem in surveys of billiard dynamics. While full hyperbolicity has been proven for many specific semi-dispersive systems (Sinai hard sphere systems, Lorentz gas, stadia, falling balls, etc.), no general result establishes hyperbolicity for all semi-dispersive tables, and the search did not find a resolution of the general question.

status_evidence.title: Hard Ball Systems and Semi-Dispersive Billiards: Hyperbolicity and Ergodicity
status_evidence.snippet: Proving full hyperbolicity (nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere) and ergodicity for semi-dispersive billiards involves crucial technical aspects studied case by case.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity of semi-dispersive billiards is established only in specific cases, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Bridge to Hyperbolic Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Physical polygonal billiards (hard disc in polygons) reduce to semi-dispersing billiards and can be hyperbolic on positive measure sets.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity of semi-dispersing polygonal-type billiards is an active and incomplete area of investigation.
